note: Questions only. Answers are graded on our server. The one-line explanations are returned by the grader after each attempt (not stored here).

quizzes.title: Stacking
quizzes.blurb: QB stacks, bring-backs and what not to pair.

questions.q: In a classic lineup, what is a stack?
choices: Two running backs from the same team
A quarterback plus his own pass catchers
Your three most expensive players
One player from every game on the slate

questions.q: What's our default stack in a classic lineup?
choices: The QB with two of his pass catchers
The QB on his own, with none of his receivers
The QB with his own running back
Two quarterbacks from the same game
Re-entering last week's winning lineup
A player coming back from injury
A second quarterback in the same lineup
A player from the other team in your stack's game

questions.q: Outside your QB stack, should you pair two teammates from another team, like that team's RB and WR?
choices: Yes, always: more teammates means more correlation
No: two teammates outside the stack split one offense's points
Only if they both cost under $5,000

quizzes.title: Ownership & leverage
quizzes.blurb: Ownership, chalk, leverage and duplicate lineups.

questions.q: A player is projected at 30% ownership. What does that mean?
choices: He'll score about 30% of his team's points
About 3 in every 10 lineups in the contest will have him
He has a 30% chance to hit his projection
He costs 30% of the salary cap

questions.q: What do we mean by leverage, or edge vs the crowd?
choices: Points per $1,000 of salary
His salary minus his projection
How often he lands in the best lineup in our simulations, minus his ownership
How many contests he's in this week

questions.q: How do we treat chalk, the week's most popular players?
choices: Fade every chalk player, every week
Play as much chalk as you can
Ownership doesn't matter, only projections do
Carry the right chalk, but never two overrated chalk players in one lineup

questions.q: You win a tournament with a lineup that nine other people also built. What happens?
choices: You split the prize money with them
You each get the full first-place prize
The earliest entry takes it all
Nothing changes

quizzes.title: Showdown captains
quizzes.blurb: Who to captain in a one-game showdown, and why.

questions.q: In a showdown, what does the captain slot do?
choices: Doubles his points at the same salary
1.5x his points at the same salary
1.5x his points, and he costs 1.5x his salary
Nothing: it's just the first slot

questions.q: Who's the best kind of captain?
choices: A player who can be the game's highest scorer
The cheapest player, to save salary
The kicker, for a safe floor
Whoever the most people are captaining

questions.q: Where does leverage live in a showdown?
choices: In a cheap flex player nobody else plays
At captain, while the popular players sit in the flex
In leaving salary unspent
In playing both kickers

questions.q: The favorite is giving more than 7 points. Where do winning captains usually come from?
choices: The underdog's pocket quarterback
The kicker
An even split between the two teams
The favorite

quizzes.title: Contests & field size
quizzes.blurb: Which contests to play, how many, and how much.

questions.q: Why do we lean toward smaller fields and single-entry contests?
choices: The top prizes are bigger
There are fewer lineups to beat, so a good read is worth more
Projections are more accurate in them
Nobody else plays them

questions.q: Over a season, which usually works better?
choices: One or two contests per slate, built around a game you believe in
Ten contests with the same five lineups in each
Every contest in the lobby, one lineup each

questions.q: A satellite pays the top 15% a seat in a bigger contest. How should that lineup look?
choices: As risky as possible, with several players under 5% owned
Leave a lot of salary unspent so it's unique
Solid and steady: a strong floor, and chalk is fine
Two quarterbacks and no running backs

questions.q: What should your weekly DFS budget look like?
choices: Double it after a losing week to win it back
Bigger whenever you feel confident
Whatever it takes to enter every contest
The same amount every week, one you can afford to lose
